tldr: Headlines across 15 of 17 buckets frame this as an unprecedented policy action — the Trump administration planning the largest-ever mass visa revocation, targeting up to 200,000 asylum seekers — while Russia and Southeast Asian outlets instead lead with a separate federal court ruling striking down Trump's 75-country immigrant visa ban.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to use the word 'Purge' — the sole punitive-enforcement characterisation in the title layer; every other outlet frames the action as a 'revocation' or 'plan', not a purge.
'Trump Admin Prepares To Revoke More Visas Than Ever Before' — the only headline that omits both the 200,000 figure and the word 'asylum', obscuring the scale and the affected population.

'Tienes visa de EU, ¿pero por cuánto tiempo?' — the only headline framed from the reader/visa-holder's perspective rather than as a policy announcement; unique reader-impact angle across all 30 titles.

'Trump verso revoca di 200mila visti. E la Corte Suprema limita il voto per posta' — the only headline that bundles the mass visa revocation with the Supreme Court mail-vote ruling in a single title, linking two distinct Trump policy stories.
Title field contains only the section label 'Internacional' — no substantive headline was captured; the spain bucket contributes no frameable signal.

bottom_line: The headline layer presents the mass visa revocation almost exclusively as a historic policy milestone — 'largest ever' — spotlighting the administration's action while suppressing the legal vulnerability and the humanitarian stakes that appear only in the bodies.
